   its clock to the final column, so it shows as a truncated `22:24:2|`.

## Acceptance Criteria

The grid is never wider than the box it is drawn in: `.xterm-screen` width
<= `.scrollback-area` clientWidth, in both chromium and webkit. Covered by an
e2e assertion so the engine difference stays watched.
close_reason: Fitted from scrollbackArea.clientWidth; e2e/grid-width asserts it in both engines

title: Сериализатор блока теряет ВСЕ цвета: colorToCSS сравнивает режим с 0/1/2 вместо масок xterm (плюс перевёрнутый порядок RGB)
description:
## Проблема

colorToCSS (frontend/src/scrollback/serializer.ts:135) сравнивает режим цвета ячейки с 0/1/2. xterm.js возвращает битовые маски: 0x1000000 (16 цветов), 0x2000000 (256), 0x3000000 (RGB, = 50331648). Ни одна ветка не совпадает → функция всегда возвращает null → в замороженный блок не попадает НИ ОДИН цвет. bold/italic/underline идут через isBold()/isUnderline() и выживают, поэтому дефект выглядит как "жирный, но белый".

Второй баг в той же функции: порядок байт RGB перевёрнут — код читает r из младшего байта (color & 0xff), xterm пакует (r<<16)|(g<<8)|b. После починки режима красный и синий поменяются местами, если не исправить и это.

Почему гейты зелёные: frontend/src/scrollback/test-helpers.ts подделывает ячейку с fgMode/bgMode 0/1/2 — фикстура повторяет ту же ошибку, что и продакшн-код, поэтому весь цветовой набор тестов проходит против терминала, не похожего на настоящий.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Запустить в nocx любую команду с цветом (например `claude` — её рамка янтарная 38;2;255;193;7).
2. Дождаться завершения и посмотреть замороженный блок: весь текст цвета текста по умолчанию.

Измерено 2026-07-28: проигрывание реального захвата PTY через @xterm/headless даёт для ячейки линейки getFgColorMode() = 50331648, getFgColor() = 16761095 (0xFFC107). E2E-прогон в приложении: span[style*="color"] = 0, span[style*="font-weight"] = 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Замороженный блок сохраняет цвета из 16-цветной палитры, 256-цветной палитры и truecolor; красный не превращается в синий.
- Тесты сериализатора идут против настоящего буфера xterm (headless-инстанс, куда записан поток байт), а не против ячеек-заглушек с выдуманной кодировкой режима — иначе тот же класс ошибки повторится молча.

title: Блок теряет хвост вывода: endLine берётся от позиции курсора, а не от последней напечатанной строки
description:
## Проблема

Замороженный блок сериализуется диапазоном [startLine, endLine], где endLine — строка КУРСОРА в момент маркера OSC 133 D (terminal-content.ts:269 → controller.ts:289 → blocks.ts:671), а не последняя строка, которую команда напечатала. Любая программа, оставляющая курсор выше конца своего вывода (типовое поведение Ink/TUI при выходе), теряет хвост блока.

У пользователя: окно доверия `claude` в живой области видно целиком, а в блоке обрывается на "Security guide" — пропадают опции и подсказка клавиш. В сыром захвате PTY teardown claude содержит ESC[1C ESC[4A (курсор на 4 строки вверх). Промпт shell перерисовывается на этой строке, а serializeRange срезает пустые строки в конце, поэтому блок кончается ещё выше.

## Steps to Reproduce

В headless-стенде (devharness + vite + Playwright), измерено 2026-07-28:

    printf "L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\nL6\n"                     → блок: L1 L2 L3 L4 L5 L6
    printf "L1\nL2\nL3\nL4\nL5\nL6\n"; printf "\033[4A"   → блок: L1 L2 L3

Тот же вывод, разница только в позиции курсора — три строки исчезли.

## Acceptance Criteria

Блок содержит все строки, записанные командой, независимо от того, где программа оставила курсор: второй случай выше даёт L1..L6. Направление — endLine по последней НЕПУСТОЙ записанной строке между C и D, а не по курсору.

title: Connections form has no validation — an empty profile saves and fails on connect
description:
The new-connection form accepts anything. Name, Host and User can all be blank; Save
writes the record and Connect hands it to the backend, which fails — so a form that was
never filled in is reported to the user as a connection error. The credential form had a
partial check behind `.cm-form-error`: one string for the whole form, unable to name the
field that failed, in `--color-error` on a surface that never defined it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Connections → "+ New connection".
2. Leave Host empty. Press Connect, then Create.

## Acceptance Criteria

Validation is a kit facility (`ui/validation.ts`) — validators plus a
show-it-yet decision — wired through `Field`/`TextField`'s existing `error` prop.
Save and Connect both refuse an invalid form, mark every failing field and raise the
first message as a toast. `.cm-form-error` is deleted. Every silent `catch` in
connections.tsx reports through a toast.
close_reason: Duplicate of the pre-existing epic nocx-74cn, which describes the same defect and the same design questions. Filed without searching the tracker first — the check AGENTS.md puts before every fix.

title: UI kit: Toast notifications with levels, auto-dismiss and sticky
description:
The kit has no notification primitive, so surfaces invent their own: the export page
renders a `.st-export-status` div under every action, which reserves vertical space
whether or not there is anything to say and pushes the layout around when there is.

Build a Toast primitive: `ui-toast-host` + `ui-toast` with `data-level`
(info | success | warning | danger), a module-level queue any surface can push to,
auto-dismissal on a per-level default, and a sticky mode that stays until the user
closes it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `showToast({ level, message, duration })` from anywhere; `duration: 0` = sticky.
- Host mounted once in the app shell; toasts stack and dismiss individually.
- `.st-export-status` and its `StatusLine` helper are deleted; export/import outcomes
  arrive as toasts.

Out of scope: pause-on-hover, undo actions, per-toast action buttons.

title: A full-screen program gets 140px of a 900px pane
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a tab and let the pane be tall — a maximised window.
2. Run `top`, or `claude`, or anything that repaints a whole screen without the
   alternate buffer.

Expected: the program gets the pane.
Actual: it is drawn into a 140px strip pinned to the bottom, with the rest of the
pane empty above it. Measured on a 1202px-wide pane: `.xterm-live-container` is
`live-running`, height exactly 140.

## Not an alt-screen defect, which is what it looks like

Alt-screen works. Proven on the headless stand: `printf \x27\\033[?1049h\x27` produces
`live-fullscreen`, a container of 1280x720 — the whole viewport — plus
`inner-fullscreen-mode`, `#app.alt-screen`, and the command block hidden.

`top` never gets there because `top` does not use the alternate buffer. Captured
from a real pty: it opens with `ESC[?1h ESC= ESC[?25l ESC[H` and repaints the
NORMAL buffer from home. Zero occurrences of `1049` in its whole output stream,
though `smcup` for `xterm-256color` is `\\E[?1049h`. Claude Code is the same by
design — it renders inline so scrollback survives.

So the class of program that suffers is exactly the one that redraws a full
screen in the normal buffer, and that class is not small.

## Cause

`style.css`: `.xterm-live-container.live-running { height: 140px }`, a constant
since a0fab46 (the DOM-scrollback commit). The live region is sized for a few
lines of command output — which is what it was built for — and a full-screen
program in the normal buffer is the case nobody sized it for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A program that repaints the normal buffer gets the height of the pane, not a
  constant.
- Ordinary short command output does not grow the live region to the full pane
  for the sake of three lines.
- Whatever decides between those two is stated in one place, with the rule
  written down.
close_reason: The live region measures the rows actually written and takes that height, capped at the scroller. No classifier: liveContentHeight reads the grid, so ls gets three lines and top gets forty. Three things had to stop fighting it, each found by measurement — overflow-anchor letting the browser adjust scrollTop as a second controller, a 120ms height transition that put every measurement mid-animation, and content-visibility with contain-intrinsic-size making an off-screen block report 48px where it was 635.

title: A credential can serve a group of hosts
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A `ProfileGroup` can carry a credential, so every profile in it authenticates
  with that identity unless the profile overrides it.
- The resolution order is stated in one place and tested: profile credential ->
  nearest ancestor group credential -> the profile inline auth override.
- The connection form shows which credential is in force and where it came from,
  so an inherited one does not look like no credential at all.
- The allowed host set for a group-bound credential is derived ON THE BACKEND
  from the hosts of that group members. The renderer never sends a host list and
  never gets to widen one.
- An empty host set stays refused, exactly as nocx-mon made it. Inheriting from a
  group is a way to enumerate several hosts, not a way back to "any host".
- Go tests: a profile in the group connects with the group credential; a profile
  with its own credential ignores the group one; a host that has been removed
  from the group is refused.

## Also in scope

Amend `docs/decisions/0006-reusable-credentials.md`. Its line 27 still documents
`empty = works for any host`, which nocx-mon made false. Group binding is the
change that makes the ADR worth rewriting rather than patching.
close_reason: Superseded by wave 2 (nocx-j685). Credential.Host no longer exists in Go; authorization is computed from the profiles that reference a credential (spec 3.1), so binding a credential to a group is not the mechanism any more. The ADR-0006 amendment this bead also carried is refiled as a bead of its own under this epic.

title: Create a credential from inside the connection form
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A `+` control sits beside the Credential select in the connection form. It
  opens the credential form in the kit Dialog, and on save the new credential is
  created AND selected in the field that opened it.
- The connection being edited keeps everything already typed into it. Losing a
  half-filled form to go and make a credential is the reason nobody makes one.
- The `Tip: Create a Credential above...` prose is deleted. It exists only
  because there was nothing to click.

## Why a button and not an option in the select

`+ New credential...` as the last option of the select is the obvious shortcut
and it misfires for anyone using the keyboard: arrowing down through the options
to read them lands on it and fires it. The affordance goes next to the control,
not inside it.
close_reason: A + control sits beside the Credential select and opens CredentialForm in a kit Dialog; on save the credential is created AND selected in the field that opened it, and the half-filled connection form survives — which is the whole point, since losing it is why nobody made credentials. The Tip prose is deleted. Not an option inside the select: arrowing through options to read them would fire it.

title: Credentials get their own settings section
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `Credentials` is an item in the settings rail alongside Clipboard, Interface,
  Export / Backup / Import and Connections.
- It lists saved credentials, and creates, edits and deletes them.
- The `Saved credentials` toolbar button on the Connections page is gone. A
  button that swaps one list for another inside a page is what this section
  replaces, not something it sits beside.
- The credential form is ONE component. The settings section and the modal from
  the sibling task both host it; there is not a second copy of the fields.
close_reason: Credentials is a settings-rail page after Connections: full-width list, kit Dialog editor, one shared CredentialForm component that wave 6 will host, delete showing its blast radius from credentials.usage, and the Saved credentials toolbar button deleted. Coordinator removed a keyboard-unreachable row click that both custom lint rules missed.

title: Credentials are a side door, not a first-class thing
description:
## What is wrong today

A credential is reachable only from the Connections page, through a `Saved
credentials` button in the toolbar that swaps the list out from under you. It has
no place of its own in the settings rail beside Clipboard, Interface, Export and
Connections, which is where a reusable identity belongs.

Inside the connection form the coupling is worse. The Credential select offers
`— None (specify below) —` and then an `Authentication (override)` block, under a
line of prose that reads `Tip: Create a Credential above to reuse auth settings
across connections.` A tip telling the user to go and do something elsewhere is
the shape of a missing affordance. There is nothing to click.

## The colleague use case that started this

A group of servers sharing one username and password. Today that means creating
the same credential once per host, because `Credential.host` is bound to a single
host and an empty host is refused at connect time — deliberately, by nocx-mon:
`"any host" is what lets this renderer aim a credential at a host it controls`.

So the answer is NOT to relax the host binding. It is to make the **group** the
unit the credential attaches to: `ProfileGroup` already exists, already has a
`defaults` bag, and already has `groups.*` RPCs. Binding a credential to a group
lets the backend derive the allowed host set from that group members actual
hosts, which is still an enumerated set the user assembled — the defence
nocx-mon added survives intact, because the renderer never gets to name a host
that is not already a saved profile.

## Note for whoever takes this

`docs/decisions/0006-reusable-credentials.md` line 27 still says `Optional: bind
to specific host (empty = works for any host)`. The code stopped meaning that
when nocx-mon landed. The ADR needs amending as part of this work, not quietly
contradicting.

## Deliberately out

Credential sharing between machines, and any change to how secrets are stored —
that is the keychain/vault boundary and it is not what this epic is about.
acceptance_criteria: Credentials have their own place in the settings rail, a connection can create and attach one without leaving the form it is being typed into, and a credential can serve a whole group of hosts without the renderer ever being able to name a host the user did not put in that group.
notes: Wave 5 of the connection-manager redesign (spec .internal/specs/2026-07-29-connection-manager-design.md section 7). Reused rather than re-created. TWO CHANGES to its original scope: (1) the '+ create a credential' affordance moves to wave 6 (nocx-uxs5), because it lives in the connection form that wave rewrites and would otherwise be built twice; (2) child nocx-0w2f.3 'A credential can serve a group of hosts' is SUPERSEDED — the credential no longer binds to a host at all, and authorization is computed from the profiles that reference it (spec section 3.1), which is wave 2 (nocx-j685). Its ADR-0006 amendment stays in scope there.
close_reason: Wave 5 landed in three commits (5b391f2, 6a46e6e, 954c4d0). Credentials is a settings-rail page with one shared form component; the Saved credentials toolbar button is gone; credentials.usage answers who spends an identity, computed on the backend through the wave-2 engine. Scope changed twice against the original epic, both recorded in its notes: .3 was superseded by wave 2 and .2 moved to wave 6. Two defects surfaced during the work and were fixed here (.6, duplicate-on-edit) or filed (nocx-nc4i reachability gate, nocx-p15s global-defaults contract).

title: The kit has no validation: forms accept anything and say nothing
description:
## What is wrong

Settings -> Connections -> the profile form takes anything. Host empty, port
blank, user empty, and Save succeeds; the row lands in the list as `?@:22` and
fails only when someone tries to connect. The screenshot the owner filed shows
exactly that row.

This is not a Connections defect, it is a missing layer. Measured:
`Field` already declares `error?: string` and wires `aria-describedby` for it,
and `grep -rn "error=" --include=*.tsx frontend/src | grep -v test` returns
**nothing**. The slot was built and no machinery ever filled it. `.cm-form-error`
is a single form-level string, which is the shape you end up with when there is
nowhere to put a per-field message.

## The design questions this epic has to answer

1. **Where do the rules live.** Two candidates, and they are not exclusive:
   - the surface declares them per field (`validate: (v) => string | null`);
   - the backend declares them, the way `settings.describe` already declares the
     settings schema, and the form renders and validates from that. This makes
     the backend authoritative and stops the two sides disagreeing about what a
     valid port is.
2. **What the kit owns.** Proposed: `Field` renders the message and sets
   `aria-invalid`; a `Form` primitive collects field state, blocks submit, moves
   focus to the first invalid field and announces the count. The surface owns
   only the predicates.
3. **Timing.** Validate on blur, not on keystroke — then re-validate on every
   change once a field has errored. Erroring while someone is still typing the
   first character is the thing everyone hates about form validation.

## Deliberately out

Async/server-side validation (does this host resolve, is this key readable) —
that is the Test-connection work, tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: A form built from kit primitives rejects invalid input before it reaches the backend, shows why against the offending field, and blocks submit — without any surface writing its own error markup. The Connections form is the proof: an empty Host, a port outside 1-65535 and a missing User are all refused with a visible per-field message.

title: The tab filter cannot be typed into — the terminal key rescue takes the keystrokes
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Switch tab placement to vertical.
2. Click the "Filter tabs" field in the strip header and type.
3. The first character lands, focus jumps to the terminal, the rest goes to the shell.

## What is happening

`TerminalContent` installs a `keydown` listener on `document` that pulls focus into the command
editor when a printable key arrives and focus is neither in the editor nor in the live xterm
container. It exists so typing works right after a click on the pane. Its whitelist was those
two places, so every other control in the window counted as not ours.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing into the strip filter, a settings field or a dialog reaches that control and stays.
- Typing after a click on the terminal pane still lands in the command editor.

title: The editor of a tab you switched away from is still painted over the active one
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a terminal tab, open a second one, switch back to the first.
2. Type. Nothing appears; clicking into the editor does not help either.

## What is happening

Panes hide with `visibility: hidden` on purpose (base.css) so their renderers keep measuring
a real size. But `visibility`, unlike `display`, is overridable by a descendant — and
`CommandEditor.show()` wrote an inline `visibility: visible` on its root. The editor of an
inactive pane therefore kept painting, pixel-for-pixel over the active one, because panes are
`position: absolute; inset: 0` and stack.

Measured on the owner page: the active pane textarea held the typed text and had focus; the
topmost painted element at those coordinates was the OTHER pane empty editor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Only the active pane paints an editor; the test measures computed visibility, not a class.
- Typing after a tab switch is visible in the field the user is looking at.
- The pane hiding mechanism is unchanged (renderers keep measuring a real size).

title: The kit has no vertical rhythm: stacked controls have no spacing of their own
description:
The kit gives a vocabulary — Button, TextField, Checkbox, FileInput, Field, Section — and no grammar for putting them one under another. `Field` spaces a label from its control; nothing spaces two controls from each other. So every surface improvises margins, and where it forgets, the controls touch.

Measured on the Export page: `.st-export-import-section` declares only `margin-bottom: 16px` (outer) and its label `margin-bottom: 4px`. The FileInput, the passphrase TextField and the "Decrypt and Import" Button below it have nothing between them at all — they render flush, which is what the owner reported.

This is a kit gap, not a bug on that page: patching `export.css` would leave the next surface to rediscover it. The kit needs a primitive that owns the rhythm (a stack with a gap from the space scale), and the surfaces need to stop declaring their own margins between controls.

Worth deciding while designing it: whether the rhythm belongs to a new `Stack`, to `Field` (every control is in one), or to `Section`'s content slot. Whichever it is, the CSS integrity gate should then be able to forbid a surface from spacing kit components by hand — that rule is what keeps this from coming back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A column of kit controls is evenly spaced with no per-surface CSS, and the Export page's import blocks are visibly spaced without `export.css` gaining a margin.
- The spacing comes from the space scale, not from a literal number.
- Every surface that improvised margins between controls is swept onto the primitive, and the ones that remain are named with a reason.
- A lint rule (or a documented reason why one is not possible) prevents a surface from spacing kit components by hand.
close_reason: Stack primitive in src/ui/stack.tsx with a two-step gap vocabulary (default/loose) drawn from the space scale — a named set, not a free token, so a caller cannot re-improvise spacing inside the kit. Section and PageSection both delegate their children to it, so vertical rhythm is declared in exactly one place. Export page's import blocks migrated to Field+Stack and export.css lost .st-export-import-section, .st-export-import-label, .st-export-passphrase-form and .st-export-btn-row entirely rather than merely losing their margins. surface-spacing-kit is rule 11, with a fixture and a both-directions gate assertion. The rule's stated limitation is real and worth knowing: a surface class WRAPPING kit children is invisible to CSS-only analysis, because the selector's subject is the surface's own class. That case is answered by the primitive, not by the linter.

title: T21: the e2e suite still drives the pre-migration tab classes
description:
T17 (nocx-olav) renamed the tab's classes when Tab became a declared feature component — .tab -> .nocx-tab, .tab-title -> .nocx-tab-title, .tab-indicator.tab-activity -> .nocx-tab-indicator[data-activity='true'] — and the close/add/caret buttons became IconButtons with no class of their own at all. Three specs were updated with it (tabs, focus-after-reorder, proof-matrix). Thirteen were not.

Measured on 23bec17: click-focus, clipboard, multi-tab-input, settings-scroll, vertical-tab-placement, activity, command-editor, enhanced-input, activity-bell, connections-settings, quick-connect, theme-switch all still name classes nothing renders. A locator that matches nothing does not report 'the class is gone', it reports 'the tab is not there' — vertical-tab-placement.spec.ts fails its beforeEach on .tab-title and reads like a broken vertical strip.

This is why it matters beyond tidiness: the epic's verification ran proof-matrix and tabs and called the browser green. Those two are exactly the specs T17 kept current. Everything the migration touched OUTSIDE them — quick-connect, the activity indicator, clipboard, the command editor, theme switching, connections — has not been observed in a browser since the rename.
acceptance_criteria: Every e2e spec selects the tab through the classes Tab actually renders (.nocx-tab, .nocx-tab-title, .nocx-tab-indicator[data-activity]) and the IconButtons through their accessible names; the whole chromium suite runs green; no spec references a class no component renders.
close_reason: Every spec now selects what the components render; 136 pass across chromium and webkit with none failing. Two assertions were vacuous rather than failing and now read aria-selected; settings-scroll was re-aimed at the one section that still overflows, with the overflow guard first so it cannot pass with nothing to scroll.

title: Rule 3: the settings nav paints a Button instead of selecting it
description:
Rule 3 progress, measured against the AST-derived identity set.

  at filing (e79e398) ........ 21 appearance declarations on a kit identity
  after nocx-etu2 work ....... 3 real ones remain

Closed:
  - the settings nav's active state — the rail painted background/colour/weight onto
    .ui-button. Button takes `selected` now, renders aria-selected and draws itself;
    the surface keeps margin-left on the badge. (2e54943)
  - the rail's chrome — background, divider and padding moved from
    `.ui-settings .ui-page__rail` into base.css. One surface was defining what every
    rail looks like. Width, flex and font-size stay: sizing and editorial choices are
    the surface's. (this commit)

What actually remains, all genuine and each a different question:

1. `.ui-settings-row .ui-field-label-col label` and `.ui-settings-row .ui-field-desc`
   (settings.css) override Field's own label and description typography — font-size,
   weight, colour. field.css already sets these, so BOTH declare them and the surface
   wins by specificity: textbook dual ownership. Needs a Field size/density variant,
   not a move.

2. `.tabstrip-vertical > .ui-icon-button { border-radius: 0 }` (style.css:260). The
   vertical strip wants square buttons. Small, but it is the surface changing a
   component's shape, so it is a variant question too.

Two of the original 21 were false positives from a line-based scan — the modified-dot
`::before` in settings.css is on a surface class, not a kit identity. Any future
measurement should parse rather than scan lines.

Still unsettled and blocking rule 3's activation: whether `padding` counts as
appearance. The design's list says yes, which makes several violations true by
definition rather than by argument. Decide it in §3.6 first — a rule that is right by
definition is the kind people route around.
acceptance_criteria: No surface stylesheet declares an appearance property on a kit identity; rule 3 is enabled in check-css-integrity.mjs with a fixture and no exemptions
close_reason: 21 rule-3 violations down to one editorial line: Button draws its selected state, Page owns its rail chrome, Field has a labelProminence variant, IconButton has square

title: Decide how a parent may position a kit component without owning it
description:
Found while landing T3 (nocx-wqrq). Gate rule 3 says surface CSS may not reference a kit identity. IconButton's consumers now do exactly that, in eleven places: .tab > .ui-icon-button, .activity-bar .ui-icon-button, .tabbar > .ui-icon-button, .tabstrip-vertical > .ui-icon-button and so on.

Most are legitimate under §3.6 — the parent owning placement — but they cannot express it without naming the child, and a couple go further than placement: .activity-bar .ui-icon-button[aria-selected='true']::before draws the active indicator, which is appearance.

Three ways out, and the choice belongs to whoever enables rule 3:
  (a) allow a parent to reference a kit identity for placement properties only, and let rule 11's property list decide which those are;
  (b) require the parent to address its own slot instead (.activity-bar > *), which is fragile but keeps the identity private;
  (c) give IconButton a variant that owns the indicator, so the surface has nothing left to draw.

Do not enable rule 3 before this is answered — it will fire on correct code, and the reflex will be to weaken the rule.
acceptance_criteria: Rule 3's treatment of parent-to-identity references is decided and written into the design spec, and T20 can enable the rule without it firing on correct code
close_reason: Decided: a parent may name a kit identity for placement only, never appearance; the discriminator is rule 11's property list. Indicator follow-up split to nocx-v177

title: The quick-connect palette offers profiles that cannot connect, and says nothing useful when they fail
description:
Two defects in one report, both seen on 2026-07-27. A profile created and never filled in ('New connection', host `?@:22`) is offered in the palette like any other; clicking it SSHes nowhere. The backend then answers 'Internal error', which tells the user nothing about what is wrong or how to fix it.

Either is worth fixing alone. An unusable profile should not be offered — or, if it is, the failure has to name the missing field.
close_reason: The palette no longer offers a profile that cannot connect — host validation rejects empty and whitespace-only hosts on the backend and the palette filter matches, with a regression test proving an empty-host profile never reaches the SSH dial. handleOpen classifies failures through classifyProbeError, the SAME taxonomy connections.test already returned, so a failure now names what went wrong instead of answering 'Internal error'. Note left open: the resize handler still answers a bare 'Internal error', which is the same smell in a different path and outside this bead's scope.

title: Command output renders on a white background in the dark theme
description:
Reported during the 2026-07-27 live UI review and reproduced on the running app, but not diagnosed — it needs computed colours read off the live page rather than reasoning about the stylesheet. Terminal content is xterm's and carries its own palette, so the suspect is the block/command-output chrome around it, not xterm.

Diagnose against a running page (cmd/devharness + the vite shim), not by reading CSS: every defect in this family so far has been valid CSS that silently stopped applying.

title: G: the browser harness for the §5 proof matrix
description: Spec §5. jsdom proves nothing about focus or layout. Via cmd/devharness (no Wails, no GTK, no display — see the e2e memory): the focus matrix for every primitive, disabled appearance per primitive, FileInput::file-selector-button, Tab/Shift+Tab and roving tabindex, theme switch with a Dialog open asserting computed token-derived colour changes without remount, scroll ownership in both modes, Page focus placement after a page change, and the rail's responsive rearrangement. Independent of the primitive spine — this is the parallelisable track.
close_reason: 60/60 browser cases; negative check confirms the focus matrix can fail; disabled-button case marked test.fail against nocx-c2t6

title: T14: Button — last, and its variant set closes
description:
Spec §3.6. Last on purpose: what `default` should look like is only knowable once the
shell's 70 variant-less call sites have become IconButton. default becomes a real
neutral button (today's secondary appearance), so secondary as a separate name
disappears and close disappears into IconButton. Done when rule 1 is enabled with no
exemptions.

FOUND DURING T1 (2026-07-27): disabled buttons have NO visual treatment today, and
never have had. kit.css:216 is `button.kit-scope:disabled` — the element-WITH-class
form — but `.kit-scope` is only ever applied to a <div> (settings.tsx:736,798 and the
dialog panel), so that selector matches nothing. There is no `.kit-scope button:disabled`
rule at all. Eight more selectors have the same dead shape (kit.css:88,106,112,139,156,
161,212,214), but each of those sits in a selector list beside a working descendant
form, so only Button is actually affected.

T1 deletes the dead selectors rather than relocating them — they are dead code and
relocating them would carry a lie into a fresh file. This transaction owes the real
rule: `.ui-button:disabled` with the opacity and cursor the other controls already get.
close_reason: ui-button + data-variant; default is the neutral button; disabled rule added; ghost variant replaces the raw button the worker introduced

title: T19: real pages — descriptors and a closed scrollMode
description: Spec §3.8. SettingsPageDescriptor carries title, description, actions and scrollMode: 'page' | 'contained'. Connections needs contained. Deletes the :has(.cm-root) detection. No Page inside a Page — the shared rail reaches each page through a thin SettingsPage wrapper. settings.tsx's root onKeyDown mixes page navigation with domain behaviour and is separated.
close_reason: scrollMode is a declared mode; :has() detection deleted; registry carries the descriptor. Focus-placement ownership filed as nocx-ln9t

title: T17: Tab as a declared feature component
description: Spec §3.7. role=tab, drag and reorder, middle-click close, activity and agent indicators, aria-controls, two orientations — a behavioural unit, not a styled button. Lives beside tab-strip.tsx with styles/components/tab.css and an entry in ui/feature-components.json. Consumes IconButton. Verified in a browser: keyboard, drag, middle-click, indicator and ARIA.
close_reason: Tab extracted as a declared feature component; 239 lines out of style.css; 37/37 e2e across four suites

title: T15: delete .kit-scope
description: Spec §4 rule 6, §6.2. The two wrappers in settings.tsx:736,798, the panel in dialog.tsx:127, and the :has(.cm-root) > .kit-scope chain in connections.css:25. The ban is on kit-scope as a JSX class and .kit-scope as a CSS selector — NOT a literal-string ban, which is unachievable: the string legitimately appears as prose in check-css-integrity.mjs:12,13,119.
close_reason: kit-scope gone from JSX and selectors; browser matrix 30/30 green

title: T20: collapse legacy style.css and enable the remaining gates
description:
Spec §4, §6.2. Measured on b7041a0, so this starts from numbers:

  style.css .................. 984 lines (1138 at the start of the epic)
  px font-size outside the
    token layer .............. 40
  surface CSS naming a kit
    identity ................. ~13, all placement

Not counted in the last figure: .ui-settings-row, .ui-settings-filter,
.ui-settings-section-nav-*. They carry the ui- prefix but no component renders them, so
the AST-derived identity set (nocx-hav2) excludes them correctly — which is precisely why
rule 3 must key off the derived set and never off the prefix. The ~13 that remain are
placement, permitted after nocx-zeti; verify each against rule 11's property list rather
than assuming, since the one real appearance case was FIXED (nocx-v177), not exempted.

## Rule 7 needs a decision about the type scale, not just a gate

The 40 px values break down as:

  13px x7   -> --font-size-sm exactly
  18px x1   -> --font-size-lg exactly
  12px x14  |
  11px x8   |  no token exists
  10px x4   |
  14px x5   |
  16px x1   |

So 8 are a mechanical substitution and 32 are not. The scale is 13/15/18/22 and the
10/11/12 cluster is "smaller than body" — badges, meta rows, captions, the tab index
pill. That is a missing step, not 26 mistakes.

Do NOT collapse 10/11/12 into one token to satisfy the gate. That is a visual change in
26 places and it needs to be looked at on a running page, not reasoned about: this epic
has already been bitten twice by CSS that was "obviously equivalent". Either add
--font-size-xs and migrate the ones that genuinely share a role, or ship rule 7 with the
remainder in its exemption list, each entry naming a file and a reason.

## Success Criteria

Every counter above reads zero or is justified in the rule's exemption list with a file,
a reason and a bead id; all eleven gates of §4 are enabled with their fixtures; style.css
holds only shell and terminal rules no component owns.
close_reason: All three criteria met. Rule 3 and rule 7 are now real gates with fixtures proven to fire in both directions, and rule 3 found five more violations on the way in — a divider drawn on the New-tab button, a Toolbar padded by the connections surface (where the kit's value was dead on specificity), a ghost Button whose padding existed only in settings.css, the page gutter owned by the one surface with a page, and the activity bar sizing the icon inside an IconButton. Rule 8's fixture is written and removed by gate.sh under a trap, because a scoped config cannot be tested from outside its scope, and it was verified to fail as well as pass. Rules 1 and 9 are recorded in §4 as deliberately not lint rules, with the argument: types refuse a class earlier and more precisely than a lint rule could, and scroll ownership is a fact about resolved layout that a static rule would have passed on. style.css is 743 -> 451 lines and holds only the shell hosts and the terminal; the 300-line move was proven not to reorder the cascade by comparing 490 competing declaration pairs, whose only three flips are between selectors no element can match both of. The px font-size counter is 18 rather than 0, exempted per the criterion with a file, a value, a count, a reason and nocx-pp3y.2 — and the exemption count is checked in both directions, so a stale entry is itself a violation.

title: T5: SearchField owns its input
description: Spec §3.1. search-field.tsx:37 currently hands the <input> an arbitrary consumer class. Two identity selectors carrying the same declarations as TextField is fine — the declarations are token references.
close_reason: ui-search-field__input; class prop removed; icon padding moved onto the input

title: T6: Select owns its element
description: Spec §3.1. select.tsx:38 emits only props.class. Native <select> with appearance:none stays per ADR-0014.
close_reason: ui-select identity; class prop removed

title: T7: Checkbox owns its label and control
description: Spec §3.1. ui-checkbox owns the row and label, ui-checkbox__control owns the box and its :checked mark — different identities, different duties, neither inferred from the other. Switch is a variant of this primitive, not a separate one.
close_reason: ui-checkbox + ui-checkbox__control; switch became data-variant

title: T2: FileInput — new primitive
description: Spec §3.5. kit.css:172-195 styles input[type=file] and ::file-selector-button through the ancestor with no component to own it. Export's two raw file inputs (export-section.tsx:330,347) adopt the new FileInput; rules move to file-input.css. The platform button TEXT stays untranslatable — that is native behaviour, not a reason to hand-roll.
close_reason: FileInput built, both raw file inputs migrated, raw-control type list widened, baselines at zero

title: T0: derive kit identity by AST, not regex
description: Spec §4. Compute the kit identity set from static class/classList literals on JSX inside frontend/src/ui/**, distinguishing root identities from __part identities, excluding comments, doc strings, querySelector arguments and variant-class tables. Replaces the regex at eslint.config.js:62, which sweeps all of those in and is not fit to bind a rule. Ships with a fixture asserting the derived set.
close_reason: AST scanner replaces the regex; kit-scope excluded as a scope marker; fixture gate asserts the derived set

title: T8: Radio owns its label and control
description: Spec §3.1. radio.tsx:23 emits only props.class and has no rules of its own in kit.css — its appearance comes entirely from catch-alls. Two live consumers: connections.tsx:357,517.
close_reason: ui-radio + ui-radio__control with a drawn dot; the .cm-radio-group label override that outranked it is deleted

title: T1: decompose the rules that span several primitives
description: Spec §6.1, §6.2. Focus ring (kit.css:6-12) moves to base.css as an application-wide invariant. The disabled rule (kit.css:212-219) is sliced ONE LINE PER PRIMITIVE, still ancestor-keyed: text/number/password, search, checkbox, radio, file, select, button. The slice list is derived from what the catch-all MATCHES, not from what the stylesheet names — .kit-scope input:disabled reaches input[type=radio], and Radio has two live consumers at connections.tsx:357,517. styles/components/ gains the empty per-component files of §3.4 and their imports. Done when the focus matrix and disabled appearance are unchanged in a browser and no rule in kit.css addresses more than one primitive.
close_reason: Split kit.css per component, sliced the multi-primitive rules, moved the focus ring to base.css; relocation verified triple-by-triple

title: T3: IconButton — new primitive
description: Spec §3.7. Genuinely repeated: tab close/add/caret, activity-bar items, dialog close, toolbar icon actions. Roving tabindex stays with the GROUP; the primitive only accepts tabIndex and selected, and requires ariaLabel. Done when no <Button class=...> remains in shell files.
close_reason: IconButton built; five consumers migrated including tab-caret and the banner dismiss; rule-3 boundary filed as nocx-zeti

title: T4: TextField owns its input
description: Spec §3.1, §6.1. Identity on the <input>, not only the wrapper. Deletes the three surface duplicates: style.css:155, export.css:200, export.css:237. Every consumer migrates in the same commit. Done when one text-input implementation exists.
close_reason: ui-text-field + ui-text-field__input; the three surface duplicates deleted

title: Explore project context (kit.css, ADR-0013/0014, nocx-pp3y, KB)
close_reason: Context gathered: kit.css, ADR-0013/0014, nocx-pp3y, KB, measured kit-scope coverage

title: Present design sections and get approval
Propose 2-3 approaches with trade-offs
Write design doc to .internal/specs/
Transition to writing-plans
Spec self-review, then user review gate
Ask clarifying questions one at a time
Brainstorming: the kit's appearance is gated on an ancestor class it never renders
acceptance_criteria: A design doc exists at .internal/specs/ and the user has approved it

title: [epic] The kit owns how controls look, and a gate keeps it that way
description:
The kit's visual contract belongs to an ancestor class the kit's own components
never render. Widened on the owner's instruction from "the kit has no default
appearance" to the whole UI except the terminal (AD-6).

Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-27-kit-owns-its-appearance-design.md (commit
d7ac36e), settled against codex over five adversarial rounds.

The measurement that decided the gate design: all three lint baselines are
already at zero and the shell bypasses the kit anyway. `<Button class="tab-close">`
satisfies "no raw button" while defeating the kit; `class="ui-export-btn"` occupies
the reserved namespace from outside; two raw file inputs sit in Export because the
ADR-0014 rule never named input[type=file].

The unit of atomicity is one primitive end to end — identity, CSS, every consumer,
the prop, the gate — never one layer, because layering guarantees an interval in
which a control is styled from two places. Children are numbered by the spec's
transaction table (§6.2).

## Success Criteria

Every kit primitive renders its own identity on its appearance-bearing element and
is styled from exactly one place; `.kit-scope` does not exist as a JSX class or a
CSS selector; `class` is gone from the visual primitives and bounded to layout on
the structural ones; Connections, Export and Settings are real Pages with a closed
scrollMode; the eleven gates of §4 are enabled and every counter reads zero.

Out of scope: a frontend/src/features/ layer, a ListRow primitive, renaming the
ui-settings-* surface classes, token values, the terminal subtree, and reopening
ADR-0013 or ADR-0014.

title: Button's default variant has no class, so 27 buttons render as native chrome
description:
`ui/button.tsx` maps the `default` variant to the empty string:

    const VARIANT_CLASS: Record<ButtonVariant, string> = {
      default: '',
      ...
    }

So a `<Button>` with neither a `variant` nor a `class` emits a bare `<button>`
and renders as native platform chrome. Found while reworking Settings: the
"Reset" button came out as a white system button on a dark surface, because
`.ui-settings-reset-btn` — the class it does carry — has no CSS either.

27 call sites use the default variant. Most of them pass a fully formed class of
their own (`.tab-add`, `.tab-close`, `.cm-save`, the activity-bar buttons), and
those are fine; the broken ones are the sites that pass neither. Simply giving
`default` a base class would push background, border and height underneath every
one of those 27 — including rules written on the assumption of a bare button —
so this needs a per-caller pass, not a one-line change.

Partially addressed already: a real `secondary` variant now exists in the kit
(`.ui-btn-secondary`) for the neutral action the kit was missing, and Settings'
Reset uses it. What remains is auditing the other call sites and giving each one
either a variant or a class.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render `<Button onClick={...}>Do a thing</Button>` on any kit-scoped surface.
2. Compare it with `<Button variant="primary">`.

Expected: a kit button. Actual: the platform's own button — light grey fill and
system focus ring, ignoring the theme.

Audit command:

    grep -rn "<Button" frontend/src --include=*.tsx | grep -v test | grep -v "variant=" | grep -v "class="

## Acceptance Criteria

- No `<Button>` in application code renders as native platform chrome: every
  call site resolves to either a kit variant or a surface class that fully
  styles it.
- A gate or test catches a Button that would fall through to bare UA styling —
  this class of defect is invisible until someone looks at the pixels.

title: Vertical tab strip lists no tabs after a placement switch
description:
With Tab placement set to Vertical, the strip mounts at its correct 240px width and
shows the new-tab `+`, but lists **no tabs** — with two tabs open, including the
active one whose content is rendering next to it.

Not yet root-caused, and deliberately not filed under nocx-u7wq: the stylesheet is a
suspect but not a confirmed one. What the static read established:

- `.tabstrip-vertical` and its child rules survived the merge intact; the only rule
  the merge dropped from that block is `.tabstrip-vertical .tab:hover`, which is
  cosmetic and cannot hide a row.
- `.tab` and friends are unscoped in `style.css` (not `.tabbar .tab`), so the base tab
  chrome does apply in vertical placement.
- The `+` sitting at the vertical *middle* rather than the bottom is consistent with
  an empty `.tabs-container`: `tabs-container` (`flex: 1 1 auto`) and `.tabbar-spacer`
  (`flex: 1 1 0%`) then split the column and the button lands between them. That is a
  symptom of "no tabs", not a second layout defect.

So the live hypothesis is that `replaceStrip()` mounts the vertical strip without
repopulating its display records — a behavioural defect in the strip swap, not CSS.
Needs runtime evidence before a fix: `cmd/devharness` plus the `NOCX_WS_PORT` shim in
`e2e/harness.ts` runs this headless, no wails and no display.

Everything else wrong in that screenshot (serif text, native selects) is already
covered by nocx-u7wq and is not this bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app with two or more tabs open.
2. Settings → Interface → Tab placement → Vertical.

Expected: the two tabs listed in the strip, active one highlighted. Actual: an empty
strip with only the `+` button; tab content still renders correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Switching placement to Vertical lists every open tab, with the active one marked,
  and switching back to Horizontal does the same.
- A test covers the *swap* specifically — mounting a strip directly was already
  covered and did not catch this.
close_reason: No longer reproduces. Measured against the running app in both chromium and webkit with two tabs open, switching to Vertical: both rows render 239x38 at y=38 and y=76, and the New-tab + sits at y=660 in a 682px strip — not at the vertical middle, which was the report's own tell for an empty tabs-container. The case the report describes was not in the suite (the existing vertical test switches with one tab and adds the second while already vertical, so it exercises addTab rather than replaceStrip); it is now, asserted by measured geometry per the nocx-d3q lesson.

title: Three stylesheets under styles/ are never imported
description:
`style.css` imports 9 of the 12 files under `styles/`. Never imported:

- `components/overlay.css` — dialog and scrim
- `surfaces/export.css` — the Export / Backup / Import section
- `themes/light.css` — tracked separately, it is the theme-switch bug

The import list is hand-maintained and nothing checks that it is complete, which is
how three files went missing in a single merge. `overlay.css` even carries a comment
explaining which token it consumes, so it was written to be loaded and then wasn't.

## Steps to Reproduce

    cd frontend
    for f in $(find src/styles -name '*.css'); do
      grep -q "$(basename $f)" src/style.css || echo "NOT IMPORTED: $f"
    done

Expected: no output. Actual: three files.

Visible symptom: the Export / Backup / Import cards in Settings render with default
block layout instead of the export surface's rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `.css` under `frontend/src/styles` is reachable from the `style.css` entry.
- A gate fails when a stylesheet is added without an import, so the list cannot drift
  again.
close_reason: Fixed in ed3a997; check-css-integrity.mjs now gates the class

title: ADR number collision: two branches claim 0013
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

    git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/feat/adr-0013-credential-trusted-endpoints -- docs/decisions/ | grep 0013
    ls docs/decisions/ | grep 0013

Observed: two different ADRs numbered 0013 — 'credential-trusted-endpoints' on that branch, 'plain-css-with-semantic-custom-properties' on ui-shell-kit-tokens.
Expected: one ADR per number.

## Detail

Noticed at merge time on 2026-07-27. ui-shell-kit-tokens lands first and takes 0013 and 0014 (component kit foundation), so the free numbers start at 0015. The credential branch is the one that renumbers, not because its work is lesser but because renumbering an unmerged branch costs one rename while renumbering a merged ADR breaks every reference already written against it.

Both branches were authored in parallel against a main that had 0012 as its highest, so neither did anything wrong. The lesson is that 'next free number' read from main is a race whenever two branches are open at once.
acceptance_criteria: docs/decisions/ contains exactly one ADR per number. The credential-trusted-endpoints ADR is renumbered to the next free number and every reference to it — commits, beads, code comments, the branch's own prose — points at the new one.

title: Forbid inline markup and CSS that duplicates a component
description:
Asked for by the owner 2026-07-27, after Page was found rendering .ui-page__body and .ui-page__rail inline while PageBody and PageRail sat unused (nocx-vxqj.9). A rule that only rejects raw <button> does not catch that: the duplication was a div with a class, and it happened inside the kit itself.

The generalisation the owner stated: no inline markup or CSS without using the component. Enforce it by deriving ownership from the kit rather than maintaining a list — a class rendered by ui/page-body.tsx is PageBody's, so any other file rendering it is bypassing the component. That check would have failed on Page the day it was written.

Pairs with the raw-controls guard (nocx-vxqj.6) and the colour grammar (nocx-xrrl.4): same baseline mechanism, same negative-fixture requirement, same rule that the baseline may only shrink.
acceptance_criteria: A check fails the build when an application surface, or another kit component, renders markup or styling that a kit component already owns. Ownership is derived, not hand-listed: for each frontend/src/ui/*.tsx the classes it renders belong to it, and that class appearing anywhere else is a violation. Inline style props are rejected in application surfaces — layout and colour belong in CSS, and the colour half is already covered by the grammar check. A negative fixture proves the rule fires by name in lint-fixtures/gate.sh. Current violations are baselined per-violation, may only shrink, and the baseline must be empty before nocx-vxqj closes.
close_reason: nocx/no-inline-markup rejects kit-owned classes duplicated outside their component and inline style props in surfaces. Ownership derived by scanning ui/*.tsx at config-load, not hand-listed, so it survives renames and new components. Verified against the motivating case: <div class="ui-page__body"> in settings.tsx fires by name and the message names the component to use. Baseline 8 across settings/connections/update-notice, growth-guarded, must be empty before the epic closes. Ten rules now fire from the negative fixture.

title: The kit contains four components nothing uses
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run, from frontend/:

    for c in PageBody PageRail Field EmptyState; do
      grep -rlE "<$c([ />]|$)" src --include=*.tsx | grep -v '^src/ui/' | grep -v '\.test\.'
    done

Observed: no output for any of the four — every consumer is a test or the component's own file.
Expected: every kit export has a production consumer, because a kit is a set of components that are used.

## Detail

PageBody and PageRail are the worst of the four: Page renders .ui-page__body and .ui-page__rail inline instead of composing them, so the same markup exists twice — once as an unused component, once by hand. That is precisely the duplication this epic exists to prevent, occurring inside the kit itself.

Field does not fit the two-column settings rows it was written for. EmptyState sits unused while connections.tsx hand-rolls 'No connections yet'.

Cause, and it is the coordinator's: the wave-1 kit brief listed which components to build from the epic's prose rather than from call sites, and the Page primitives were each commissioned separately without requiring Page to compose them. The rule this epic was founded on — do not create a component per need, check who will call it first — was broken by the brief that created the kit.

Supersedes the framing of nocx-vxqj.7 and nocx-vxqj.8: there is no 'two categories' question. A component nothing uses is a defect; a consumer the kit does not serve is a missing component. Both are fixed by making the inventory equal the consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Every component exported from frontend/src/ui/ has at least one production consumer, verified by a check that fails otherwise — the same shape as the raw-controls guard. No surface and no kit component renders markup a component already owns: Page composes PageBody and PageRail rather than rendering their divs inline. Field either fits the settings row it was written for or is replaced by a component that does, and that component is used everywhere it fits. EmptyState is adopted by every surface that currently hand-rolls an empty state. Components are not deleted to satisfy this — consumers adopt them.
close_reason: All three baselines empty. Field gained orientation and is adopted by settings rows; Button gained a close variant and rest-props and the chrome buttons in banner/sidebar/tab-strip/update-notice are kit components; Radio added for the connections auth group; EmptyState adopted. Every kit export now has a production consumer. The ui- namespace is documented as reserved for component-owned classes, with kit-scope as the consumer-applied marker.

title: Quick-connect: a modal picker from the caret beside +
description:
Decided by the owner 2026-07-27 after weighing the activity bar, a dropdown on +, an overflow menu, and integration into the command editor. See design spec section 2.4 for the reasoning, in particular why a modal beats a dropdown here: it needs no Menu or Popover primitive (which ADR-0014 declines to build for want of a consumer), the platform supplies focus trap and Escape, it scales past a handful of hosts, and it is the seed of the command palette rather than a single-purpose surface.

Depends on the overlay work in nocx-vxqj.5 because the native <dialog> wrapper, the focus-return-to-xterm path and the Wails drag-region guard all belong there.
acceptance_criteria: A caret beside the tab strip's + opens a modal built on native <dialog>, listing the local shell and every SSH profile, filtered as the user types, opening a tab on Enter or click. Keyboard: the filter input has focus on open, arrows move the selection, Escape closes and returns focus to the caret. It reaches tm.newSSHTab() by the same path the old Connections surface used, proved end to end. A keyboard shortcut opens it without the mouse. The component is written so that connections are ONE SOURCE of its list, not the whole of it — the command palette reuses it.
close_reason: Quick-connect modal on the native dialog, opened from a caret beside + and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P. The list is a provider interface returning {id,label,detail,run} so a command palette adds a second source without touching the component. 12 e2e pass in both engines. Coordinator: the guard rejected the caret as a new raw button and the regeneration script refused to grow the baseline, so Button gained a tabIndex prop and the caret became a kit component — the first evidence that the kit CAN cover chrome controls, which informs nocx-vxqj.8.

title: ADR-0012: Remove Bind to Host из credential editor UI
description: Credential create/edit form contains authentication identity only: name, username, auth mode, key metadata, secret-write actions. Remove Bind to Host and binding port. Connection form remains the place where host+credential are associated. Trusted endpoints may be shown in credential details as read-only derived information, but not a free-form editor. While connection references a credential, username/auth mode/key selection come from that credential — no silent override.

title: ADR-0012: Schema migration legacy Host/Port → TrustedEndpoints
description: Profile document schema gains new module version. Migration reads legacy Host/Port before ordinary decoding discards them. For each credential+profile: resolve canonical endpoint; if legacy host non-empty AND matches endpoint under legacy port semantics → create profile-sourced grant; if empty/mismatches/unresolvable → no grant, mark profile as requiring review; do NOT broaden automatically. Remove legacy Host/Port only after migrated document is durably written. Export/import uses same versioned migration, must not silently turn legacy unbound into wildcard.

title: ADR-0012: CanonicalEndpoint resolver (единый owner)
description: Credential grants, enforcement, dialing, host-key lookup, errors, pool keys consume the same immutable CanonicalEndpoint. Calculated after SSH config: explicit profile values > ~/.ssh/config (HostName, Port) > SSH defaults (port 22). Host and port separate validated fields. Ports outside 1..65535 rejected. DNS case-insensitive canonical; IP literals (incl IPv6) parsed+canonical. SSH alias = display metadata only, not authorization identity. DNS lookup results and CNAME targets NOT persisted as grants. If ~/.ssh/config changes alias to different endpoint → existing grant no longer matches → connection fails closed.

title: ADR-0012: Тесты верификации (полный набор из ADR)
description: Тесты покрывают: (1) one credential assigned to multiple profiles+exact endpoints; (2) arbitrary ungranted host+port refused before auth; (3) SSH aliases, effective ports, IPv4, IPv6 canonicalization; (4) assignment, reassignment, host edit, unassignment, profile deletion, idempotent save; (5) target and jump-host credentials independently; (6) profile save rollback when grant persistence fails; (7) grant fields+secret references rejected/preserved across renderer CRUD; (8) revocation before fresh dial AND pooled channel open; (9) complete profileId→resolver→session→SSH path (no auth fields dropped at module boundary); (10) migration of matching/empty/mismatching/unresolvable legacy bindings; (11) host-key trust independent from credential endpoint authorization.

title: ADR-0012: Revocation affects future opens + pool reuse
description: Removing/replacing a grant prevents all subsequent opens, including new channels on existing pooled SSH transport. Existing active channels allowed to run until closed (does not terminate live shell on profile edit). Pool security identity includes canonical endpoint + credential ID + authorization revision + authentication policy + jump-route identity. Pool hit still performs current grant check before opening channel. Secret rotation and grant mutation advance relevant revision so new open cannot reuse transport authenticated under stale authorization.

title: Export section speaks the same page and section vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: The export section renders through PageSection and kit components with no raw interactive controls and no st-export-* rules duplicating kit styling. Its 25 local signals are reviewed against the ownership table: transient state stays local, anything accepted and shared moves. Existing export/import behaviour is unchanged, proved by the existing tests.
close_reason: Export renders through PageSection and the kit; all 11 raw-control violations gone, 25 createSignal collapsed into 5 local stores (nothing shared, per the ownership table), 256 lines of dead st-export-* rules deleted. Guard baseline 21 to 10. No assertion changes needed. No e2e covers export, stated rather than invented.

title: Delete the standalone Connections surface
acceptance_criteria: SURFACE_CONNECTIONS, SINGLETON_CONNECTIONS, connections-content.ts and the connections tab registration are gone, along with cm-* rules superseded by kit and page classes. The reachability test from .3 still passes. No SSH capability is lost: profiles, groups, credentials and Tabby import are all still reachable and tested.
close_reason: Standalone surface removed: connections-content.ts, SURFACE_CONNECTIONS, SINGLETON_CONNECTIONS, SURFACE_ID_CONNECTIONS and its registration, the wrapper-only test, and the .cm-header/.cm-keys-list rules that existed only for it. connections.tsx survives as the Settings page. Verified: exactly two classes lived only in the deleted stylesheet and neither is used by the surviving page. tsc clean via the local binary (npx cannot resolve tsc in worktrees — a brief defect, now fixed in the skill), 777 unit tests, 69 e2e pass. Worker retracted its own worker_done over the npx gate, which was correct behaviour on a requirement I wrote wrong.

title: Connections added as a Settings sub-page, every entry path exercised
acceptance_criteria: A Connections page is reachable from the Settings rail and covers profile CRUD, groups, credentials and Tabby import. An end-to-end test walks from the activity-bar gear to a created SSH tab through tm.newSSHTab(). Draft lifetime, request cancellation and observer ownership on sub-page navigation follow the state ownership table from nocx-82l9.7. Nothing is deleted in this bead: the standalone surface still works.
close_reason: Connections is a page in the Settings rail via the typed registry; nothing deleted yet (nocx-imkb.4 owns that). e2e walks gear to a created SSH tab and passes in WebKit. Guard baseline 29 to 21, connections.tsx 10 raw controls to 2, both window.confirm calls now the kit dialog. Worker correctly raised a decision gate rather than touching main.tsx; the one-line wire applied inside the factory so a fresh SettingsContent gets it before mount. Coordinator repaired: unparsable JSX (missing nav/ul opening tags), a page registry typing a component page as a bare Component when it needs props, an orphaned handleSectionClick, and the worker's own e2e asserting .cm-header which its migration had replaced with a kit Toolbar.

title: Settings on Page and the kit, with a typed page registry
acceptance_criteria: Settings renders through Page plus kit components with no raw interactive controls left. The rail is a typed registry of generated pages (one per Go-declared section) and explicit component pages. The generated-screen invariant holds inside generated pages: adding a Go setting still costs zero frontend changes, proved by a test that adds a declaration and asserts it appears. scrollToKey uses PageScroller.scrollToElement, not row.scrollIntoView. The settings screen scrolls at a short window height in WebKit.
close_reason: Settings composes Page, PageRail, PageScroller and PageSection, takes every control from the kit, and its stylesheet has zero colour literals. The rail is a typed registry of generated and component pages — the seam Connections needs. Generated-screen invariant proved by a test that adds a declaration and asserts the nav entry. scrollToKey uses PageScroller.scrollToElement. Coordinator repointed the e2e selectors that the migration invalidated, including ones in specs the worker did not own, and widened Button's children to JSX.Element. Finding kept: Field does not fit two-column settings rows, which is a gap in the kit.

title: Page primitives and the two named scroll owners
acceptance_criteria: Page, PageHeader, PageBody, PageRail, PageScroller and PageSection exist with the CSS contract from spec section 6.1. PageScroller is the single content scroll owner and exposes scrollToElement(); PageRail scrolls only as a bounded rail and does not scroll independently at the narrow breakpoint. A test asserts a page subtree contains no computed overflow auto/scroll node other than those two. SidebarView provides the same header/filter/body composition for panel views.
close_reason: Page, PageHeader, PageBody, PageRail, PageScroller, PageSection and SidebarView exist with the height contract; PageScroller exposes scrollToElement. Scroll ownership is two named owners with a test that fails on a third overflow container. KNOWN LIMIT, recorded honestly by the worker: the invariant test runs in jsdom, which applies CSS from style elements but computes no layout, so it catches a structural violation and cannot prove the chain holds under WebKit. Follow-up filed.

title: Frozen scrollback is snapshot-themed, and keeps its algorithmic colour conversion
acceptance_criteria: ANSI 0-15 come from the theme; indices 16-255 and truecolor stay algorithmic content conversion in scrollback/serializer.ts. The active palette is injected at capture time so a later theme change does not recolour already-frozen blocks. Tests cover a theme change before a block freezes and after.
close_reason: TerminalSnapshot (palette + defaultFg + defaultBg) threaded through the serializer; blocks.ts captures it at freeze so a later theme change does not recolour frozen output. ANSI 0-15 from the theme, 16-255 and truecolor algorithmic and byte-identical. Colour literals live only in DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT. This is the redo — the first attempt reported 82 passing tests while the file did not compile, and was reverted; tsc --noEmit now exits 0 and is required by every brief since.

title: xterm reads the same tokens, with the startup race closed
acceptance_criteria: One adapter builds xterm's ITheme from the resolved --terminal-* properties; the literal palette at renderers/xterm.ts:152 is deleted. A synchronous bootstrap resolver runs before the Solid render and before any terminal is constructed: it applies data-theme, validates that every required property resolves non-empty, and falls back atomically to the built-in theme otherwise. A concrete ITheme is passed into terminal construction, never read opportunistically afterwards, and theme-change subscription is registered before construction or reapplied immediately after. applyTheme is a terminal-controller operation that also performs whatever refresh or atlas invalidation xterm needs; ADR-0005's refresh pump stays inside the controller and is never driven from reactive state. A Linux WebKitGTK test asserts a live terminal repaints in the new palette with no user input.
close_reason: One adapter builds ITheme from --terminal-* tokens; the literal palette in renderers/xterm.ts is deleted. Synchronous bootstrap resolver runs before the Solid render with atomic fallback; concrete ITheme passed into construction; subscription registered before mount. applyTheme is a controller op that forces the refresh, with ADR-0005's pump untouched. CRITICAL finding from the worker: all 21 --terminal-* tokens were absent from the theme file — nocx-xrrl.2 never wrote them and the coordinator's brief asserted they existed. Added here from the shipped palette and all 21 verified in WebKit. reconcileThemeFromGo is wired but uncalled: ui.theme is not declared in internal/settings yet.

title: State and derived colour tokens: hover, active, selected, disabled, focus ring, overlay
acceptance_criteria: Every interaction state has a token, defined per theme or derived centrally once in tokens.css; no component defines its own hover shade and none uses opacity on a whole element as a substitute. Focus-ring, scrim/overlay and translucent-selection tokens exist. If color-mix() is used, the WebKit floor from the ADR is respected and a fallback is present.
close_reason: Satisfied by the state-colour correction in nocx-xrrl.2: every interaction state — hover, active, selected, disabled, focus-ring, scrim, translucent selection — is a token assigned in the theme. No component defines its own hover value; all reference var(). color-mix() is not used for these, so the WebKit floor does not apply and no fallback is needed. ADR-0013 §3.1 records why derivation was abandoned.

title: The colour grammar check: a parser, not a hex denylist
acceptance_criteria: A CI check parses CSS declarations and permits, outside themes/, only var(--token), currentColor, transparent, inherit, and color-mix() whose every colour operand is one of those — so named colours, oklch(), lab(), color(), gradient stops and box-shadow colours are all caught, and color-mix laundering a literal is rejected. It also scans JSX style props and SVG fill/stroke attributes. Current violations are enumerated in a baseline that may only shrink and must be empty before nocx-xrrl closes.
close_reason: ESLint rule for JSX style props and SVG attributes plus a css-tree scanner for CSS declarations; permits only var(), currentColor, transparent, inherit and color-mix over those, and blocks the color-mix(..., red 20%) laundering case. Its first act falsified the token migration's 'zero literals outside themes/': ten exist — six in overlay.css inside var() fallbacks, four in connections.tsx inline styles, both invisible to a CSS-file grep. Baselined, not fixed. Coordinator declared css-tree, which was present only transitively.

title: styles/ split: tokens.css plus tokyo-night extracted from the existing 27 colours
acceptance_criteria: frontend/src/styles/ contains tokens.css, themes/tokyo-night.css, base.css, components/ and surfaces/. The 27 unique colours currently in style.css are expressed once in the theme file and referenced by token everywhere else. The rendered application is pixel-identical to before, proved by screenshot comparison in WebKit. style.css no longer carries a palette.
close_reason: styles/ now matches ADR-0013: tokens.css, themes/tokyo-night.css, base.css, components/, surfaces/. 265 colour literals became var() references; zero remain outside themes/. Coordinator ran a computed-colour diff in WebKit that the worker could not, and it found five real changes hiding in a refactor advertised as mechanical — tab bar, vertical strip, settings rail, clipboard banner and active tab had been collapsed into shared tokens. All five restored as their own tokens. The remaining diff is color-mix() serialisation only. ADR-0013's surface-hover derivation was proven wrong (the real hover is darker than the surface) and the ADR is corrected.

title: ADR: styling architecture — plain CSS with semantic tokens
acceptance_criteria: An ADR in docs/decisions/ records: plain CSS with semantic custom properties in frontend/src/styles/, with Tailwind and CSS Modules weighed and rejected for stated reasons; the token layers (semantic UI colour, control metrics, terminal); the allowed colour GRAMMAR outside themes/ rather than a literal denylist; the policy for colours that never appear in a CSS file (Go settings, xterm's injected stylesheet, serializer output, SVG assets); and the minimum WebKit version supported for any color-mix() derivation, with the fallback if that floor is not met.
close_reason: ADR-0013 records plain CSS with semantic tokens; Tailwind and CSS Modules declined with reasons; allowed colour grammar instead of a hex denylist; color-mix floor WebKitGTK 2.40 / macOS 13.1 with a generated @supports fallback. Coordinator fixed two self-contradictions (white/black mix anchors, rgba scrim) and settled the theme bootstrap-cache rule in 8.1.

title: The guard: raw controls and direct Kobalte imports rejected, with a baseline that only shrinks
acceptance_criteria: An ESLint rule rejects raw button, select, textarea and checkbox/radio inputs, and any @kobalte/* import, in application surfaces; frontend/src/ui/ and terminal-owned files are exempt by explicit path list, never by surface-wide waiver. A machine-readable baseline enumerates every current violation by file and control; CI fails if the baseline grows. nocx-vxqj cannot close while the baseline is non-empty.
notes: Reframed 2026-07-27. The guard must not blindly reject native controls now that the ADR may deliberately adopt <select> and <dialog> inside kit wrappers. The rule stands for APPLICATION SURFACES — raw button/select/textarea/checkbox/radio there is still a violation — but frontend/src/ui/ is where native implementation details are allowed to live, by path exemption rather than by surface-wide waiver. The @kobalte/* import clause only applies if a library is adopted at all; if none is, drop it rather than leaving a rule against a dependency that does not exist.
close_reason: Custom ESLint rule nocx/no-raw-controls rejects raw button/select/textarea/checkbox/radio and innerHTML in application surfaces; ui/ and terminal-owned files exempt by explicit path. Per-violation baseline, growth-only failure, deliberate regeneration script. Negative fixture proves all 8 rules fire by name via gate.sh. Coordinator regenerated the baseline after the Settings migration: 39 to 29, and the 10 that went are exactly Settings' — the guard and the migration agree independently.

title: Kit wave 2: overlay primitives behind wrappers, with the Wails portal contract
acceptance_criteria: Select, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip and Combobox are exposed as nocx components; no app surface imports @kobalte/* directly. The wrappers own the portal root element, the z-index layer scale, --wails-draggable:no-drag on that root, the dismissal policy and focus return to the invoker. Packaged WKWebView and WebKitGTK tests open every overlay type from the title-bar region and from a terminal-adjacent surface and assert the control activates rather than dragging the window.
notes: Reframed 2026-07-27. The original criteria treated all six primitives as equivalent portaled overlays behind one library; they are not. Per primitive now: modal dialogs use native <dialog> + showModal(), which renders in the browser top layer and is therefore EXEMPT from the portal-root and z-index assertions while still bound by the drag-region, focus-return and xterm-textarea clauses; Popover, Menu and Tooltip are custom overlays sharing one portal root AND one overlay stack, so Escape closes only the topmost; Combobox is NOT built until a real consumer defines its contract (editable vs select-only, local vs async, free-form values, grouping, virtualisation, form semantics). Add explicit keyboard and ARIA acceptance for Menu: roving focus, Arrow/Home/End, typeahead, disabled items, submenu direction and delay, focus return, context-menu coordinates. Packaged drag/focus tests remain required for every custom overlay.
close_reason: Native <dialog> behind a kit wrapper plus an overlay core: stack (Escape closes topmost only), portal root, focus return, --wails-draggable no-drag guard. terminal-content.ts's paste confirm migrated; connections.tsx:166/:178 and settings.tsx:610 left for their file owners with exact replacements listed. Coordinator fixed floating promises, test typings, and pointed tabs.test.ts at the kit helper. NOT verified and recorded as such: packaged Wails drag interaction and xterm focus-return in a real webview.

title: Kobalte spike: pinned version, measured gzip, portal behaviour in a packaged webview
acceptance_criteria: Reports the exact @kobalte/core version, its publication date, maintenance status and declared peer range against solid-js 1.9.14. Reports the MEASURED raw and gzip delta against the real production build: shared-core cost once, plus incremental cost per primitive for Select, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tooltip and Combobox. Reports a packaged WebKitGTK run opening each overlay type from the title-bar region and from a terminal-adjacent surface, stating drag-region behaviour, stacking, focus return and dismissal. Ends with a recommendation and a named fallback if any check fails. No production code is merged from this bead.
notes: REOPENED 2026-07-27 by coordinator after an adversarial review of the spike. The bead was closed prematurely and its headline number is not what it is labelled. Three defects in the measurement, none of them the worker's fault beyond method: (1) primitives were built CUMULATIVELY with Select FIRST, so the '34 KB shared core' contains Select's own dependencies — @internationalized/number, collection machinery, live announcer — and a Dialog-only build may include almost none of it; the report therefore cannot conclude Dialog+Popover+Tooltip costs 34+3.2 KB. (2) The production baseline and the harness were SEPARATE builds and the delta was added arithmetically; section 4.1 required measurement against the real production entry. (3) No packaged WebKitGTK run and no Wails drag interaction, both of which 4.1 required. Also: the coordinator misquoted the budget — ADR-0012's 25-35 KB is a NET allowance against which the migration already spent +7 KB, so +34 would exceed the ceiling by about 6 KB, not consume all of it. Redo measures each primitive INDEPENDENTLY, then the intended combinations, against the real production entry with a Rollup metafile attributing gzip by package, and compares against a local implementation that RETAINS @floating-ui/dom where collision-aware positioning is genuinely needed.
close_reason: Redo measured each primitive independently against the real production entry with by-package attribution: Dialog +11.6 KB gzip, Tooltip +17.4, Popover +20.9, the three together +23.7; ContextMenu +30.5, Select +31.7, Combobox +33.6; Corvu dialog +4.1. Native <dialog> confirmed available at our floors (Safari 15.4 era, below the 16.2 floor); HTML Popover API is Safari 17 and therefore above it. The first spike's 34 KB was Select's dependency closure charged to everything after it. Packaged Wails run still NOT done — blocked by webkit2gtk-4.1 with no 4.0 available; filed separately. Scripts preserved at .internal/measure/ so the numbers can be re-derived.

title: Kit wave 1: the components we write ourselves
acceptance_criteria: Button, TextField, SearchField, Checkbox, Field, Section, Toolbar, Badge, EmptyState and Toggle exist in frontend/src/ui/ with tests covering keyboard operation, focus-visible, disabled and invalid states.
